#4141. Beyond Gaming: The Essential Software Every PC Gamer Should Have

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, G2A.COM.

As console prices continue to rise, more people are turning to PCs for their gaming needs than ever before. The trouble is, PCs, and the components you need to make them run well, are getting pretty pricey too. It’s more important than ever to try and make your PC do everything you want it to do for less, and that means focusing on the software rather than the hardware.

Whether you have a top-of-the-range PC that could be performing even better, or a PC with lower specs that you want to get more out of, having the best programs and software installed is key. Below you’ll find five essential pieces of software that should be installed on every gaming PC, all of which are currently available at G2A.COM for less.

Windows is the operating system that everyone thinks of first when they hear the term OS. The thing is, not all versions of Windows were created equal. Windows 11 is great, particularly for gaming, but if you really want to harness all of your PC’s power and all of its RAM, you really should be using Windows 11 Pro.

Windows 11 Pro supports PCs with up to 2TB of RAM. That’s almost 16 times more than the standard Home version of Windows 11 can handle. It also boasts a Remote Desktop feature that allows you to log in and control your gaming PC hub from any other device in the house. An incredibly useful feature for gamers who hop between devices based on what they’re playing and where they prefer to play it.

VPNs are becoming more and more commonly used by just about everyone. If you have a gaming PC but you don’t have a VPN, you’re doing yourself a disservice. You should have one for a multitude of reasons, and if you’re going to get one, then you may as well make it the industry standard, NordVPN.

VPNs can protect gamers from DDoS attacks, whether they be the kind that target entire games and studios, which are unfortunately becoming more common, or the kind that focus on you, courtesy of a disgruntled rival you may have bested in an online lobby overreacting to their defeat. A VPN also means you can bypass regional restrictions and grab games that might not be available in your part of the world.

As for why NordVPN, the gold standard offers military-grade encryption that offers better security and protection than just about any rival VPN on the market. It also offers two additional security protocols so that even the actions between your PC and the VPN itself can be masked.

As touched upon when discussing NordVPN, security on your gaming PC is of the utmost importance. Particularly in the present day when pretty much all games require you to be online - even most of the “offline” single-player ones.

You’d be surprised how many people simply leave their PC security up to the programs that come pre-installed. They’ll protect you to an extent, but if you want to fortify your virtual walls and really make sure nothing sneaks through, you should invest in Bitdefender Total Security.

Bitdefender is always running in the background, keeping your PC safe from any threats while not compromising your system’s performance. It is second to none when it comes to detecting malware, and best of all for this topic in particular, it has a dedicated Game Mode. Turn that on, and Bitdefender will never interrupt you while you’re playing.

Have you ever been playing a game on your PC that should look and run a lot better than it does? Or been sitting with a new game in your virtual cart, wondering if your setup will be able to run it at its best? Well, there’s software for that. A program that will test everything about your PC and its capabilities that checks back in with you to let you know what it can handle, or why it can’t handle what you expect from it.

That program is called 3DMark. 3DMark can check in on all sorts of internal details and potential issues with your PC that let you know where you might need to upgrade, or what needs to be fixed. It will automatically let you know what your PC’s ideal benchmark is, estimate how games will perform based on those results, and monitor important variables such as CPU temperature, speed, and framerate.

For millions of you, playing games online with others doesn’t just mean online multiplayer. It means streaming your gameplay for the world to see, potentially to massive audiences, and most of the time while you talk over your gameplay and engage with your audience.

Whether you want to sound a little different while you do that, change your voice entirely, or just make your streaming sessions more entertaining, there’s Voicemod Pro. Voicemod Pro uses AI technology to mask and alter your real voice, with an entire library of different voices to choose from. There’s also an expansive soundboard with a suite of various noises for you to pepper in throughout your streams. That’s where that added element of entertainment comes in courtesy of VoiceMod Pro.

#4140. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4139. Poll: Which Dr. Mario & Puzzle League Box Art Is The Best?

We are back with another edition of Box Art Brawl!

It was a Zelda blowout last time, as we matched up every cover from Ocarina of Time across its various releases. Somewhat surprisingly, the newest Switch 2 design took the win quite comfortably with 31% of the vote — it could be recency bias, but it really is a rather lovely cover.

With Europe and North America opting for the same look on this one, we've got a good old East vs. West match-up on our hands.

There's no misunderstanding what's included in this game, eh? The Dr. Mario cover is up the top, the Puzzle League one is below. A red line bisects the pair with a clear bit of "2 games in one!" text for anyone who misunderstood the cart's contents up to that point. Hey, it gets the job done.

The Japanese cover goes for something a touch more abstract, and we like it! The dual logos along the bottom make it clear what's included, of course, but the game covers have been replaced by some cool dotted art. Hang it on the wall!

Thank you for voting! We'll see you next week for another edition of Box Art Brawl!

#4138. 10 Great Games That Defined The Xbox Series X|S

Eric Warner is a Journalist and Multimedia Producer based in New England with over 7 years of experience producing stories for multiple publications

It’s rare for gaming brands to last through three console generations, let alone four. Microsoft’s gaming brand, Xbox, has managed to do just that, reaching the momentous milestone of creating gaming memories for 25 years.

However, Xbox’s fourth and current console generation, the Xbox Series X|S, has been impacted by an ongoing identity crisis for the brand, with Xbox initially focusing on acquiring studios, Game Pass, and Play Anywhere, only to lay off hundreds of employees and refocus on developing exclusive titles.

Despite that rocky history, there were still many great exclusive and Microsoft-supported games that launched on the Xbox Series X|S and showcased Xbox’s ever-changing priorities.

In 2014, Microsoft acquired Mojang and the greater Minecraft franchise. Since then, Microsoft has been striving to expand the Minecraft franchise through spinoffs like Minecraft: Story Mode, Minecraft Dungeons, and, for the Series consoles, Minecraft Legends.

Developed by Mojang and Blackbird Interactive, Minecraft Legends is a cross between traditional action games and RTS titles, having players acquire resources and mobs like Golems to defend the world against invading Nether forces.

Like many Minecraft spinoffs, Legends’ reception was overall mixed between critics and gamers, but its unique gameplay style goes to show just how much endless potential the Minecraft franchise has beyond its humble survival origins.

The British video game developer Ninja Theory soared into gaming prominence with the release of the ambitious action-adventure game Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice, but that game’s success wound up being a blessing and a curse: NT was acquired by Microsoft shortly thereafter in 2018.

Since then, Microsoft helped fund and publish the MOBA Bleeding Edge as well as Hellblade’s sequel, Senua's Saga: Hellblade II, which followed series protagonist Senua once again as she sets out to free her people from captivity in Iceland during the ninth century.

While Hellblade II would receive critical praise for its story and gameplay just like its predecessor, its success was apparently not enough for Microsoft to continue investing in NT, with the developer now facing closure and a third Hellblade game facing cancellation.

Double Fine is well-known for creating some of the most creative and hilarious games of the 21st century. They also have a long history with Xbox, having released Psychonauts as a timed original Xbox exclusive and Iron Brigade as an Xbox 360 exclusive.

However, Double Fine briefly joined Xbox Game Studios in 2019 to release Psychonauts 2 and its first Series X|S exclusive, Keeper, a very unique adventure game following a living lighthouse as it sets out to help a bird called Twig reunite with its flock.

Despite its rather bizarre, Dr. Seuss-like nature, Keeper wound up being a very fun, visually wondrous, and heartwarming game that every Double Fine fan and Series X|S owner should give a try, even if Double Fine is no longer a part of Xbox Game Studios.

From Project Gotham Racing to Halo: Combat Evolved, these 10 great games defined the original Xbox and set the groundwork for Xbox's future.

Bethesda and Microsoft have often worked together to release some of the best RPGs as timed exclusives on Xbox consoles, such as The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, but their relationship solidified in 2020 when Microsoft officially acquired ZeniMax Media and its studios including Bethesda.

This led Microsoft to make Bethesda’s first brand-new RPG in years, Starfield, a timed Series X|S exclusive. The game takes place in the early 24th century in Alpha Centauri human colony worlds and sees players join Constellation, the last group of space explorers.

While Starfield turned out to be not as impressive as similar space-based games like No Man’s Sky and The Outer Worlds, it still managed to deliver engaging FPS combat and third-person spaceship piloting, as well as a wide variety of customization options for the Spacefarer, ship, and bases.

In 2023, Microsoft made the record-breaking acquisition of Activision Blizzard for $75.4 billion. Since then, most Activision Blizzard games have been optimized and intended for Series X|S play, with one of Activision's best games released under Microsoft ownership being Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

The fourth and final entry in the 2019 Call of Duty: Modern Warfare reboot series, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 features a campaign split between Captain John Price hunting down Vladimir Makarov and South Korean soldiers fighting a North Korean invasion.

MW4 is easily the best Call of Duty campaign released in years, ending the new MW series in an arguably far better way than the original MW3 and hopefully setting the stage for more great COD campaigns to come in the near future.

Obsidian Entertainment is famous for creating some of the best RPGs ever made, such as Fallout: New Vegas and South Park: The Stick of Truth, but recently they’ve increasingly become known for creating some of the most fun survival multiplayer games, such as Grounded 2.

Set two years after Grounded, Grounded 2 sees the same kids from the first game once again shrink down to the size of insects as they struggle to survive in the public Brookhollow Park, where grass now appears like a vast jungle and spiders are monolithic predators.

Grounded 2 is still in early access, but that doesn’t stop it from being one of the most fun multiplayer games to play on Series X|S consoles, with players being able to explore and craft in over eight distinct biomes on foot or by tamed bug mounts.

The Xbox had a rough start, but it managed to stick the landing in the industry and our hearts with these great games.

As a part of ZeniMax’s acquisition, Microsoft also acquired the Sweden-based MachineGames, famous for developing the new Wolfenstein series of games. In 2024, it released one of the most surprising hits of the current console generation, with Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

Released as a timed Series X|S exclusive, Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is a primarily first-person adventure game, following the famed archaeologist in between the first and third movies. He sets out to discover the secret behind the global Great Circle before his enemies do.

While Indiana Jones and the Great Circle doesn’t have Harrison Ford reprise his iconic role, it’s easily the best Indiana Jones story to appear since 1989 and is a pure fun, pulp adventure that any fan of Steven Spielberg and George Lucas’ movies will enjoy.

The Xbox One era was a rough time to be a Halo fan, and sadly, the Series X|S era wasn’t much different. Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries, only released one brand-new Halo game on the platform: Halo Infinite.

The sixth mainline entry in the Halo series, Halo Infinite sees Master Chief attempt to defeat the now tyrannical Cortana on Zeta Halo, only for the Banished from Halo Wars 2 to ambush the UNSC. Master Chief, a Pelican pilot, and a new AI called The Weapon must attempt to defeat the Banished alone.

Infinite may have launched without Forge, campaign co-op, and a lack of several multiplayer modes, but it still wound up featuring a fun multiplayer that aimed to return the series to its more classic roots. An emotional campaign story set in the series' first true open-world setting on Zeta Halo, it's not to be missed.

From PUBG: Battlegrounds to Cuphead, these 10 great games defined the Xbox One and helped entertain players through Xbox's darkest era.

For 44 years, Microsoft has stood as an innovative pioneer in the realm of flight simulation games, through its long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series. In 2024, Asobo Studio and Microsoft released the most realistic and visually impressive entry yet, with Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

A direct follow-up to 2020’s Microsoft Flight Simulator reboot, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 features much of the same core gameplay as its predecessor, but with a ton of new additions such as an in-depth career mode, dynamic environmental events and wildlife, and a plethora of new aircraft to fly such as airships and gliders.

Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is easily one of the most relaxing and awe-inspiring games to play in the Series X|S era, as people can fly practically any aircraft they want in first or third-person all over the globe. Iconic locations including Zion National Park, Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, Rio de Janeiro, and more are available as awe-inspiring sights.

Without a doubt, the best game that truly defines the Xbox Series X|S era and showcases the power of the console, as well as the potential future of the Xbox brand, is The Coalition's Gears of War: E-Day.

The sixth mainline entry in the Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game, Gears of War: E-Day has players once again embody the iconic duo of COG soldiers Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago, as they witness the Locust’s first attack on humanity in the city of Kalona on Emergence Day.

Returning to the franchise’s gritty, more horrifying roots, E-Day is to many Xbox fans the best Gears game since Gears of War 3, as it not only features an epic yet somber campaign but features a highly addictive multiplayer spearheaded by the new PvE mode Horde Siege. Every element of the series at its best.

From Kinect Star Wars to Halo 3, these 10 great games defined the Xbox 360 and the era when Xbox was at the top of the gaming industry.

#4137. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4136. Minecraft Dungeons II First DLC 'The Humblers Awaken' Arrives Next Month

Mojang hosted a surprise Minecraft Dungeons II broadcast at TwitchCon San Diego this year, and alongside this, it's announced the first paid DLC will be arriving very soon.

The Humblers Awaken will launch on 1st December 2026 and brings a fresh adventure to the action-RPG with new quests, unexplored environments, colourful cosmetics and an expanded arsenal of gear. Here's a bit more about what you can expect:

"The Sift is in danger once more, and the humblers – an ancient threat that has slumbered for ages – are beginning to wake up. Turns out they are not particularly happy about it, and if left unchecked, they will spread across the dimension, or worse – stir a much more dangerous foe. It falls on you and your trusty allies to venture into the dimension’s deeper reaches and investigate this strange unrest.

"The journey will take you through the sprawling fungal sporefields and winding underground burrows, with new quests shedding light on the mystery behind the humblers’ rude awakening."

This DLC will also add "three new artifacts that provide active abilities" and "four new talismans offering passive bonuses". Additionally, there's some cool new equipment including The Pearl skin, the Baby Nuzzle pet and Nacreous cape.

Alongside this DLC will be a bonus free update - this will add new challenges, more weapons and armour to Minecraft II. It will also reunite heroes from the original Minecraft Dungeons (Hal, Hex, Adrienne and Valorie) as player skins. There'll also be the new trial dungeons, where you can earn powerful gear:

"Take on the new trial dungeons to earn powerful gear. Available through Brave Haven, trial dungeons offer daily and weekly challenges that feature a combination of rule-bending modifiers and increased difficulty. Enormous spiders, constant TNT explosions, and soul projectiles are just some of the modifiers you will encounter in these dungeons!"

Last but not least, it's been confirmed the DLC 'Illusions of Grandeur' will launch at some point in Spring 2027.

#4135. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4134. How To Claim Every Free Xbox 25th Anniversary In-Game Item

Xbox has had one of the most tumultuous years in its history. Ongoing mass layoffs, a leadership overhaul, and studio closures have plagued what was supposed to be a year celebrating its 25th anniversary. The brand has attempted to try and mark that occasion in good ways too, the latest of which is by giving those who continue to use its consoles and play its game some free stuff.

The anniversary celebrations have been ramped up this week as Sunday, November 15 marked exactly 25 years since the launch of the original Xbox console. To celebrate, Xbox revealed seven rewards you can claim across its biggest games, from unique new armor to green guns, and we’re going to run you through how to claim all of them.

It wouldn't be a proper anniversary without a splash of nostalgia and teases for new projects to come.

Halo seems like a good place to start since, along with the original console, it’s the series that started it all for Xbox. Halo: Campaign Evolved has a new armor set that makes Master Chief look like he’s wearing pieces of the new translucent green Series X25 consoles.

Now that the console has sold out for a second time, Campaign Evolved’s Damascus Prototype armor might be the closest you ever get to owning one. It’s incredibly easy to claim too. All you have to do is log in to Halo Waypoint using the email address connected to your Xbox account and enter the code GWT9-DNBT-7X9S-DJCX-8KH3 (thanks, Pure Xbox).

If you would rather just have your gun coated in Xbox green rather than your entire protagonist, then you’ll want the rewards up for grabs in Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 instead. To get E-Day’s Anniversary Weapons Skin set, all you need to do is go to the in-game store and claim it.

Modern Warfare 4’s reward is a little different and, unfortunately, the only one of the six that requires you having to spend some money, at least if you don’t already own the game’s Vault Edition. If you have the edition, you should get the blueprint automatically. If you don’t, you’ll have to purchase the Vault Upgrade to get it.

Back to the completely free rewards, you can celebrate Xbox’s birthday in Minecraft by claiming the OG Green Character Creator Item through the Minecraft dressing room. Hop over to Forza Horizon 6, and you’ll find the GR GT Anniversary Livery. Another one that’s easy to claim, as it should be waiting for you in the game’s Gifts tab.

The full list of all seven Xbox anniversary rewards can be found below. You will need to claim them before December 1, 2026.

#4133. KFC is Inviting You to a Funeral so You Can Play GTA 6

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

There are only two days left until the landmark launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which promises to be immensely profitable for Take Two. The gears of society are already starting to grind to a halt as the world braces itself for a statistically-significant portion of the population to disappear into their homes for an indeterminate period. There’s probably going to be at least one guy in a small town out there somewhere who thinks he’s become the last man alive when he doesn’t see anyone on the streets.

It’s kind of an open secret that everyone who plans to play GTA6 will be ditching work or school on the 19th. Many workplaces around the world are aware of this, and some have even done the sporting thing and given their employees an unofficial holiday for a couple of days rather than trying to work without them. Unfortunately, not everyone has managed to secure an iron-clad excuse, but that’s where a certain purveyor of chicken is stepping in.

On the official Instagram account for the Australian arm of fast food chain KFC, it was announced that everyone’s totally real best friend “Ann Alibi” has tragically passed away, and by sheer coincidence, her funeral will be held on November 19. This isn’t just a marketing stunt; an actual funeral will be held, coincidentally providing the perfect out for anyone in need of a day off.

Arion Kurtaj has pleaded guilty to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack that leaked Grand Theft Auto 6 footage and source code.

The post on the KFC Australia Instagram features a photo invite memorializing the passing of “Ann Alibi,” with an invite reading, “It is with heavy hearts, and a much lighter workload, that we announce Ann finally got her wings. She was always there for us when we needed her, in sickness, and in perfect health. By remarkable coincidence, her service will take place on the very same day something thirteen years in the making finally arrives.”

The invite adds that a service will be held from 11:00 AM, and urges attendees to “please let your manager know.”

By remarkable coincidence, her service will take place on the very same day something thirteen years in the making finally arrives.

The real-life funeral will be held at KFC’s Robina, Queensland location, and will include “a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest."

Anyone who attends the service in person will be treated to some complementary chicken, but for everyone who can’t be there for, y’know, whatever reason, will be able to livestream the event online. Plus, KFC’s Australia locations will be offering free delivery all day on the 19th.

KFC is offering just about every semi-realistic avenue for turning this obviously-fake funeral into a genuine excuse for a day off, with the aforementioned book of condolences being the perfect way to create a paper trail for those in need of an excuse for a day off.

"We appreciate that Australians have responsibilities, but some occasions are simply too important to miss," a KFC Australia spokesperson said in a statement obtained by Australian business outlet Human Resources Director. "And in accordance with Ann's final wishes, we've made sure the funeral takes place during working hours."

Surveys suggest that around 12 million Americans are planning on either adjusting work schedules or taking PTO, though given the sheer size of this launch and its accompanying social movement, it wouldn’t be especially surprising if many players didn’t even bother to concoct an excuse.

Some workplaces know that trying to corral employees away from GTA6 would be a foolhardy endeavor, and as such, aren’t even bothering. Palworld developer Pocketpair recently announced that all of its employees are getting time off from Thursday to Monday, just to keep friction to an absolute minimum.

GTA VI will be one of the biggest video game releases in our lifetimes, and it will be talked about for years to come.

#4132. Mega Man: Dual Override Reveals Robot Master Design Contest Winner

Capcom has announced the winner of the Mega Man: Dual Override Robot Master design contest, with the winning character set to officially appear as an in-game boss.

In a video hosted by director Shinya Ikuta and producer Hiroyuki Minamitani, the pair showcased the six finalists before revealing that the winner is... Cleanser Man!

Submitted by artist 'iregyuradabii', Cleanser Man was chosen as the winner "after many discussions and careful consideration", with Ikuta-san stating that the selection process was "incredibly difficult for the entire team". The remaining finalists will have their names appear in the in-game credits.

All of the 6 finalists had some really great and unique ideas, and the entire dev team has been very impressed and amazed at the amount of creativity on display.

It wasn't easy picking a winner, but we ended up deciding on Cleanser Man due to his whimsical motif and unique color pattern.

The lid part on the detergent has a very Mega Man-esque design to it, and we like that the detergent itself is very colorful as well.

You have to be careful not to introduce too many elements to prevent the design from becoming too cluttered, so we like that the artist kept things relatively simple.

But there's still enough detail to it to give it that genuine Mega Man feel.

Once again, thank you to everyone who joined in the contest.

We really appreciate the time and effort everyone put into this.

And here's a look at Cleanser Man. Be sure to check out the video above to see it in action:

Mega Man: Dual Override is scheduled to release on Switch and Switch 2 in Spring 2027. So far, five Robot Masters have been announced, including Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, Cook Man, and the prize-winning Cleanser Man. There are still three left to reveal, so we'll keep a close eye on future announcements.

#4131. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4130. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4129. Random: Modder Transforms DS Into A Home Console, And It's Super Cool

We have long pondered what a DS library would look like on Nintendo Switch Online for some dual-screen, big-screen action. Nintendo is yet to give us the real deal, so modder KOUZEX has taken things into his own hands, creating a build that converts our beloved clamshell into a full-blown home console. And yes, it's super cool.

The above video introduces the DualStation, a mod build that combines an original DS motherboard and a bunch of unique components into a system that boasts quite an impressive array of features. We're talking full 60Hz HDMI output, touch controls via just about any means you can think of (controller, mouse, Joy-Con, drawing tablets), Bluetooth controller support, a built-in mic and a bunch of other bells and whistles.

KOUZEX's introduction video showcases the full build process before highlighting the system's widescreen gameplay, screen swapping and more.

It runs original DS and GBA cartridges, too, so there's still that sense of classic home console tactility that we all know and love.

The modder plans to sell both self-install kits and pre-built systems at some point down the line, providing options for those who know their way around a soldering iron and those who don't.

It all looks really rather wonderful in practice. As rumours of DS/3DS games on NSO continue to rumble away in the background, it's wild to see someone go all-out with some proper home console flair.

#4127. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4125. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4124. Devolver Digital Runs Free Game Contest Asking People To Delete GTA 6

Forget games being praised for releasing in the same month as GTA 6 - there’s an indie game bold enough to launch on the same day. Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed launches on November 19, and if you delete your GTA 6 preload, Devolver Digital might give you the game for free.

For years, Devolver has joked that it would release a game on the same day as GTA 6. Even when GTA 6 got delayed (twice), Devolver altered course along with it. Turns out it wasn’t a joke either, as here we are with two days to go, and Volvy’s Adventure, published by Devolver, will launch on the same day as what might end up being the biggest video game ever.

GTA 6 has consumed so much of the oxygen in the video game room that, predictably, getting people excited about Volvy has been nigh on impossible. It’s entirely likely this is the first time you’ve even heard of it. That’s why Devolver is turning up the heat and bringing out the big guns by giving Volvy’s Adventure away for free - but only if you delete your GTA 6 preload.

While everyone else is avoiding GTA 6, Devolver Digital is coming out swinging

“Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA 6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam,” the post on Devolver’s Twitter reads. It’s even paired with a clip of someone, presumably from the publisher's team, showing you how it’s done, which honestly, after how long it took my terrible internet to download all 212 GB of it, sent a shiver down my spine.

To be clear, if you like the look of Volvy’s Adventure and you’re seriously considering deleting GTA 6 for it, doing so doesn’t guarantee you’ll get a copy for free. Removing GTA 6 from your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S merely enters you into a giveaway to be in with a chance of getting Devolver’s new game for free, and there has been no indication of just how many copies the publisher plans on handing out.

Volvy’s Adventure is also the polar opposite of GTA 6 when it comes to launch platforms. While Rockstar’s big game will only be available on consoles, Volvy’s Adventure is exclusively available on Steam. If you don’t have a PC or a Steam Machine, then deleting your GTA 6 preload and sharing the evidence with Devolver will, at best, get you a Steam code that’s useless to you. Hey, maybe you can give it to a friend.

If you don’t have GTA 6 loaded up already, Devolver did offer one person the chance to enter by sharing evidence of them biting into a raw onion. I’m unsure if that offer is open to everyone.

It’s also worth noting to those in awe right now that might not fully understand what’s happening here that Devolver isn’t asking you to delete GTA 6 and throw away $80 for the chance to win a game that costs a fraction of that price (it’s $3.74 right now). Once the preload has been deleted, you can just re-download the game. The thing is, a game that big takes a long time to download, and at this late stage, depending on your internet speed, the longer you leave it, the more risk there is of GTA 6 not being ready to play when it unlocks in your region.

The theory that codes in boxes are being used to avoid leaks at all costs just became a little bit more credible.

#4123. "BioWare's closure represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy" argues petition calling on Canadian government to step in

1,662 Canadians have been verified as signing it thus far

Calls for the Canadian government to help ressurect recently shuttered RPG makers BioWare have progressed from a single post by a politician to a petition with enough signatures that it looks set to be presented to the Canadian House of Commons for an official response. So far, 1,662 people from the country of maple syrup and also other things have signed this call for their leaders to consider stepping in.

"BioWare is one of Canada's most important cultural exports to the world in the 21st century, selling tens of millions of units of their video games globally," declares the petition, started by Brendan Routh and authorised by Vancouver Kingsway MP Don Davies.

"BioWare's productions champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights that are at the centre of Canada's national identity," its run of bullet points continues. "BioWare has been shuttered by its American parent company Electronic Arts, now owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners and BioWare's closure represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy."

With all of that in mind, the petition calls on the Canadian Government to "provide BioWare with the capital necessary to secure independence of themselves and their intellectual property from Electronic Arts and resume business as an independent, Canadian company". The Canadians who've signed also want their leaders to "protect Canadian businesses and cultural institutions from being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests" and "champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada's national identity by preserving BioWare's invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry".

Thus far, the petition's amassed 1,662 verified signatures from citizens across Canada, putting it above the 500 verified signature threshold required for it to be presented to the country's House of Commons. That'll be followed by the tabling of an official response from the Canadian government.

As with some of the responses from political bodies the likes of the Stop Killing Games campaign have gotten over the years, I find it hard not to see this petition not being greeted with an answer along the lines of 'We do care about this and thank you for raising it, but we're not really gonna do much here'. I think a full BioWare resurrection with government backing is highly unlikely, but finding some way to enshrine the studio's legacy or contribution to Canada's games industry and arts culture seems a lot more easily doable.

A big statue of Blokeshep and Femshep surrounded by their crew of potential allies somewhere in Edmonton, maybe. Or a big stone middle finger that's always required to be aimed at a poster for the next Star Wars film/game/TV show/bit of merch.

#4122. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4121. Guide: Pokémon Pokopia Apples to Applin Event Guide, From Syrupy Apples To A Kitchen Table

Cor! Five new Grass- and Dragon-types for a limited-time only

The Apples to Applin event runs from 16th November to 1st December, 2026, adding five Gen 8 Pokémon to Pokémon Pokopia.

If you've played previous limited-time events, you'll know what to expect. A new Pokémon, Applin, will drop outside the Pokémon Center, asking you to find a currency (Syrupy Apples) in exchange for new items, helping you construct several brand new habitats.

This Pokémon Pokopia guide explains how to start the Apples to Applin event, how to get Syrupy Apples, and everything you need to find Applin evolutions Flapple, Appleun, Dipplin and Hydrapple.

On this page: Pokémon Pokopia Apples to Applin Event Guide, From Syrupy Apples To A Kitchen Table

Before you start, you need to have rebuilt a Pokémon Center. Once done, make sure you have the latest update, and are playing between the dates of 16th November to 1st December, 2026.

As with recent live-events in the second half of the year, you couldn't time travel to this event ahead of time. But once the start date has passed and once you've connected the game to the internet to authenticate the date, you are able to time travel back if you missed it.

Either way, when you log in during the above dates, Applin will appear outside of the Withering Wastes Pokémon Center and ask for you Syrupy Apples. Once you have enough, you can then trade them for event-specific items inside a Pokémon Center, and build three unique habitats.

To get Syrupy Apples, you must visit Dream Islands with the help of Drifloon by interacting with a doll.

Once in a Dream Island, look for apples growing on trees; give them a headbutt and collect your spoils.

You'll find around 40-50 per visit, meaning you'll need to visit on another day to get 80, which is enough to buy one of every event item (or if you're simply unlocking the event habitats, then you just need 70).

Alternatively, can grow your own Syrupy Apple Tree by buying Syrupy Apple Seeds during the event - one of which is a requirement for one of the habitats - if you so choose, allowing you to source Syrupy Apples in a location of your choosing.

When you have some Syrupy Apples, you can head to the Pokémon Center and exchange them at the counter for event-specific items. These are:

The Apples to Applin event has three habitats to unlock:

This means you need to acquire a total of 70 Syrupy Apples to get items for three Habitats.

Unlike past events, this isn't a simple case of buying and combining the items, as the Abundant Apples and Apple Kitchen requires some additional prep and / or other items first.

For Abundant Apples's Syrupy Apple Tree, plant a Syrupy Apple Seed tree in soil prepared with the Rototiller, then water it each day until it grows and sprouts fruit, turning it into a Syrupy Apple Tree.

This will take around three to four days in total, though you can always change the time to do this quicker, and is definitely not what we did to speed up the process.

As for Apple Kitchen's Kitchen Table, if you don't have one already, you can find one of these in the building on the edge of the water west of the Pokémon Center in Bleak Beach (see the mini-map in the below screenshot for the exact location). From there, you can use a 3D Printer to copy a couple more.

Best of luck getting all three habitats before the event wraps!

#4120. You can now play Pillars of Eternity and Pillars of Eternity 2: Deadfire with a controller on PC from start to finish, thanks to a new update open for testing

Deadfire’s turn-based mode has also gotten a makeover

After gifting Pillars of Eternity a turn-based mode for its tenth anniversary, Obsidian have now rolled out full PC controller support for both the RPG and its younger sibling Pillars of Eternity 2: Deadfire. The support, along with some tweaks to Deadfire's turn-based mode, are currently out in public test form.

"You can now play the whole of either game with a controller, from character creation to the end credits (and, in Deadfire, all the way out to naval combat), in both real-time with pause and turn-based mode," the studio wrote in their announcement of the public test going live. "Deadfire’s support builds on the controller scheme from the console editions. Prefer to switch things up? Pick up your mouse and keyboard at any time, and the game follows right along."

"Deadfire’s turn-based mode has also been reworked with the improvements we made for Pillars of Eternity’s turn-based mode: turns now follow each character’s speed, combat is more lethal, and swapping weapons or drinking potions no longer costs your action. You can now switch turn-based mode on or off during a playthrough, and the update brings a long list of fixes across combat, quests, audio, and the interface."

Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are included in the support, along with the Steam Deck and Steam's Big Picture mode. Radial menus have been worked in to allow rapid firing of abilities, spells, and party commands, with the interface also popping up the right button prompts for your controller of choice.

These additions are all part of Patch 1.3.10.0, the full notes for which can be found in the post I've embedded above, alongside instructions on how to get into the public test. The patch also does things like ensure "the description of Fulvano’s Boots is no longer fragmented". I'm glad Obsidian have saved those soles.

The studio haven't put a concrete end date on the test at this point, instead noting it "will run for some time as we continue to update it in preparation for a full release". As it's a test, those jumping in should expect bugs and other funkiness.

#4119. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4116. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4115. Goddess of Victory: Nikke's PC launcher suffers potential malware infection, with its publishers suggesting folks who've booted since late September do a security check

A cruel twist for the Shift Up-developed epic shooter RPG of cruel humanity destiny

Goddess of Victory: Nikke, a gacha shooter/RPG developed by Stellar Blade makers Shift Up, has suffered a "security incident" which has seen its PC launcher potentially be infected with third-party malware. Thankfully, it seems a patch to make the launcher safe again has been quickly dished out, but publishers Level Infinite are still advising players who've booted the game up since September 27th to do some security checks.

"We have identified that some files in the NIKKE Windows PC launcher were recently tampered with by a third party, potentially allowing malicious programs to run when the launcher was launched," the developers of the game with anime girls who - judging by the promo art - breast boobily announced yesterday. "As a result, your PCs and account information may have been exposed to security risks.

"We are continuing to investigate the extent of the potential damage and review appropriate response measures. We are also conducting a thorough review of our network security environment, including our CDN, to determine how the PC launcher files were compromised. We will take all necessary precautions to prevent further damage and ensure that this issue does not happen again. We deeply regret that this security incident has caused Commanders significant concern and distress, when our responsibility should have been to provide a safe gaming environment."

In order to try and help players "scan for and remove the malicious programs distributed in this incident", publishers Level Infinite have added a feature to Nikke's official PC client that does just that. They're advising that anyone who's booted up the game at least once after September 27th at 15:41 (UTC+9) use that or perform a manual security check.

Once that's done, affected players are advised to change the passwords for any accounts they've used on the PC they used to boot the launcher, as well as generate new API keys and access tokens. "We take very seriously the possibility that this incident may have affected not only your gaming experience but also your PC, accounts with external services, and personal assets," Level Infinite added. "If you believe you may have been affected by this issue or suffered from any loss, please contact our customer support team. We will review each inquiry carefully and respond as promptly as possible."

Going forwards, they plan to improve their monitoring "so that any unauthorized file modifications or security threats can be detected early and addressed promptly", as well as "establish an integrity verification system for external resources accessed by the PC launcher" and ensure the launcher only requires "the minimum permissions necessary".

Here's hoping the studio are able to keep things more secure in the future and that affected players are able to get rid of any malware with minimal suffering or inconvenience.

#4114. Nvidia ensure unboxing a ludicrously expensive new graphics card isn't limited to real life in these RAM crisis times by releasing a GeForce 8800 GTX unpacking sim

Hey at least the card in this bit of 2006 nostalgia bait has only cost you a virtual arm and leg

In what feels a fairly cheeky move during a time when memory shortages have infamously made it pretty much impossible to buy a decently powerful new graphics card without spending approximately a gazillion pounds/dollars/dollarpounds, Nvidia have decided to put out a Steam demo that allows folks to re-live the feeling of unboxing a ludicrously expensive graphics card in 2006.

The demo, dubbed GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend, has been developed by Dylan Browne. He previously made Through The Ages, a "real-time high end graphical cinematic that takes us on a nostalgic journey through three of NVIDIA's iconic GPUs" which is also on Steam for reasons.

The GeForce 8800 GTX demo, as you might've guessed, is a tribute to that specific card in the form of a tech demo simulating what it was like to unbox one in a mid-2000s bedroom. Seriously, there's a copy of Crysis on the desk so you know this is the domain of a true devotee to the best graphics available in around 2007.

"Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower," the demo's description declares. "Explore nods to GeForce history and hidden easter eggs as DLSS 4.5 with Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, path tracing, and Mega Geometry bring the nostalgic setting to life. From holding the card to the glow of the monitor, rediscover a moment in PC gaming history - or experience it for the first time!"

As the GeForce 8800 GTX was a top-line card that cost $599 on release in 2006 - about $1,000 in today's money if the online inflation calculator I've just used is on the money - this isn't really a 'we know cards are ludicrously expensive right now, but here's a reminder of when you used to be able to actually afford to unbox one' sort of demo. It is at least a free way to virtually experience having blown a chunk of your savings on something that can render really sexy textures without the existential dread of doing so in real life.

Well, I say that, I've just noticed the minimum requirements for the demo note that you'll need an RTX 4070 card. So, depending on your current setup, this might well be a case of Nvidia offering the chance to render unboxing a card you couldn't afford in 2006 via a card you can't afford in 2026.

Is that about the best we can all hope for in 2026? Probably.

#4113. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.
