#4112. Review: Mobapad M12 Pro Joy-Con For Switch 2 - The Best Option For Handheld

Mobapad's M12 HD Joy-Con for Switch 2 were exceptional. They are, in many ways, superior to Nintendo’s official offering, largely thanks to the ‘smooth-gliding’ TMR sticks, satisfying mechanical inputs, and comfortable design.

Yet with the absence of mouse controls, I found myself returning to the console’s default Joy-Con 2 until they once again became my go-to options. To be clear, I rarely use mouse mode, but the knowledge that I couldn’t was enough to sway me.

The new M12 Pro Joy-Con eliminate almost every issue I had with their HD predecessors. Available for pre-order at $119.99 (down from the regular price of $149.99), they include every feature from the official Joy-Con 2 – yes, everything. So you’ve got NFC support, 9-axis gyro, mouse controls, a proper ‘C’ button, and HD rumble that feels just as good as the real deal.

Add in the TMR sticks, a proper D-pad, and remappable back buttons, and you’ve got a pair of Joy-Con that, if you can stomach the price, are unquestionably the best option for handheld play.

Since I’ve already reviewed the M12 HD, I’ll focus primarily on the new features in the Pro.

Review Mobapad M12-HD Controllers For Switch 2 - A Clear Step Above Nintendo's Joy-Con 2

To start, the Joy-Con use Switch 2 protocol for connection, meaning the console recognises them as official Switch 2 accessories. This allows for instant connection, no faffing around with pairing settings, and of course, wake-up support with a simple click of the Home button.

Utilising the Switch 2 protocol also ensures that NFC support is always active and not reliant on a Bluetooth toggle, while the Pro now also sports a dedicated ‘C’ button – the HD’s use of a macro to navigate to the Chat app was fine, but a proper button is much better.

Finally, the little on-screen animation when you snap the Joy-Cons in place actually matches the new colour scheme (purple and green), so that’s a lovely little touch.

Mouse mode is perhaps the biggest surprise. I wasn’t expecting any third-party Joy-Con to include this for a while, but to see Mobapad pull it off so well is awesome. Like the official Joy-Con, you can use mouse controls on multiple surfaces, including a pair of jeans, and it remains accurate with minimal lag. What’s more, the ergonomic shape of the M12 Pro means that mouse mode actually feels reasonably comfortable for a change.

Using the face buttons and analogue stick at the same time still feels a tad awkward, but I actually feel like I can grip the Joy-Con properly while moving it across a surface. I can’t say the same for the official Joy-Con 2.

Rumble has also been upgraded. Officially dubbed ‘HD Rumble 2.0’, you can adjust the intensity via controller shortcuts, and it feels incredible. I don’t know if it’s exactly on par with the official Pro Controller, but it’s pretty damn close. In fact, you’ve probably seen videos of the Pro Controller’s rumble matching the tone of the ocarina in Zelda: Ocarina of Time. It’s remarkable stuff, and the M12 Pro does the exact same thing.

In terms of features, those are your main upgrades over the M12 HD. The design, however, has also been slightly changed. In terms of colour, you now have a gradient going from black to purple, and it looks really nice in person. I am, however, conscious that this won’t be to everybody’s taste, so I’m hopeful that Mobapad provides some expanded options in the future.

The darker colour scheme also ensures that, like the HD, the Pro accumulates a few marks over time from fingerprints. It’s not quite so noticeable on the upper purple sections, but you might want to give them a little wipe-down from time to time. Again, some lighter colour options will help to mitigate this.

The last change to highlight is the light-up Mobapad logo located at the bottom of both Joy-Con. I didn’t mind this on the HD, but the logo has been shrunk down drastically on the Pro, opting instead to feature a cool pattern that shimmers with the RGB lighting. It’s a lot more attractive, and looking back on the HD’s logo reveals just how garish it really is. If you’re not keen, however, you can disable the RGB functionality entirely via the Mobapad app.

Mobapad’s M12 HD was already a compelling alternative to Nintendo’s official Joy-Con 2, but its lack of mouse support meant that it failed to become my default option. Now, with the M12 Pro sporting every feature from the Joy-Con 2, including mouse controls and improved HD rumble, I genuinely can’t imagine using anything else.

If you’re someone who enjoys playing the Switch 2 in handheld mode but finds the official Joy-Con lacking in comfort, the M12 Pro will prove a sound investment. It doesn’t get much better than this.

The sample used in this review was provided by Mobapad.

#4111. Apex Legends adds a grumpy, teamwiping Godzilla to its growing history of unappealing crossovers

No doubt eager as peas to help pay off EA's billions in debt, battle royale shooter Apex Legends is set to run another of its intellectual propertytastic crossover events. This one, starting on November 10th, stars Godzilla, of Godzilla Minus Zero, Godzilla vs. Kong, Godzilla (1954), Godzilla 2000: Millennium, Godzilla (1998), Son of Godzilla, and Godzilla (2014). I might be missing some.

Besides a profitable range of weapon and character skins, most of which appear to have hot glue gunned an 70-year film franchise's worth of dorsal fins all over themselves, the King of the Monsters himself will show up on the game's Storm Point map. He does at least have more than a background cameo: he'll occasionally blast an area with Legend-melting atomic breath, though brave souls who risk the danger zone can score a custom Devotion LMG with a unique heat ray attack of its own.

Worth noting also that the character skins are each based on a certain 'zilla movie, though as our freelance news writer and associate Large Lizard Cinema expert Ashley isn't working today, I'm not sure which of these are from hits and which are the duds. Walking wallhack motherfucker Bloodhound gets the newest fashion, their skin being inspired by Minus Zero, while my personal favourite Scottish scientist Horizon gets duds based on Big G in Godzilla vs. Destoroyah. Octane's skin is taken from... something called a Jet Jaguar? Google suggests this may in fact be elite Godzilla knowledge, something I clearly lack.

Regardless, and with the understanding that a lot of effort goes into these crossovers, I still kinda wish they didn't exist? Even putting aside basic game-playing problems with how, for example, wacky skins interfere with Legend silhouettes – you couldn't pay me to initiate a fight against a full team of near-identical Gundampeople - it's just icky to have an otherwise sharp, smart, at times fiercely competitive battle royale turned into an animated billboard for a few days.

Besides, Apex already has its own kaiju: the sleepy, pacifist Leviathans that innocently wandered into the King's Canyon map for a few of the earlier seasons. I consider these much better Friend Material than Godzilla, on the grounds that they'd only kill you by accident, and it was usually your own fault - by wandering under their briefly raised megahooves - anyway.

#4110. The Legend of Khiimori's Mongolian Expanse update brings in frosty mountains and scorching deserts that'll require a lot more than a fur coat and a sturdy horse

Another day, another opportunity for some horsing around! I'm being literal here, to be clear, as a new update for The Legend of Khiimori dropped yesterday. It's called The Mongolian Expanse, opening up the map a whole lot more and making a sweep of other additions to the game.

Previously, you might have looked out unto the snowy mountainscapes and the scorching deserts and thought "boy howdy am I glad I can't go there, those temperatures look like a nightmare to deal with!" Well, good news, as you now can head to those locales, each with "their own waystations, Yam nodes, named places, chests and bandit caches."

You don't want to wander there without some amount of prep, however, as the mountains are cold and difficult to climb, with wolves none too kind to humans like you. The desert, of course, is really hot, for both you and your horse. Both additions remind me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its use of extreme temperatures acting as a sort of challenge gate. Neat stuff!

The buck doesn't stop there with this update though. You'll find a whole host of new wildlife, ranging from wild boars, to gobi bears and camels. Of course, a horse game wouldn't be one without more horse, which there is! It's a new breed called the Marwari, a horse that is "built for endurance and especially resistant to heat, a strong partner for long, punishing Desert crossings." Beyond that, you'll also find more than 60 new horse skills, all findable across specific regions and for specific breeds.

It's a nice beefy update with plenty more tweaks, additions and fixes on top of everything mentioned above. When it comes to the mountains and desert, you can also expect some big additions there, as this is only the first part of this update. You can read about everything else the update offers right here on Steam.

#4109. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4108. 'That's An Error' - Xbox Engineer Denies 360 Games Are Being Teased For Disc To Digital

Update [Fri 13th Nov 2026, 5:45pm]: Well, unfortunately we have answer - Xbox engineer Eden Marie has confirmed over on BlueSky that the inclusion of Fable III in this image was an "error".

While the post itself is private, it reads as follows (and thanks to Pure Xbox user TheBillConiglio for alerting us to this):

"Bill: Seeing an image of a library with Fable 3 having a disc to digital badge. Error, or......"

Original Story: Yesterday, Xbox starting rolling out three new console features for Xbox Insiders to try out: rotating home backgrounds, the ability to choose which side the Xbox guide pops open on, and new ways to organise disc to digital games.

They're all cool features that we're definitely keen to play around with, but what got our attention most was the image Xbox used to show off the new disc to digital update. Particularly, the games featured with the D2D licence icon plopped in the bottom-left corner of each game tile.

Did Xbox just tease the inclusion of Xbox 360 games in the D2D programme? Well, that would be true if the image depicting Fable III is to be taken at face value. At a glance, you'd probably see the image above and think, 'great, that's awesome', but the more you look at it, the weirder it gets.

Avowed famously launched on Xbox without a physical disc. So, if the theory about Xbox 360 games joining the programme is on the money, does that mean we're getting a physical copy of Avowed too? And what about Age of Empires IV? That never received a physical release either. Then If we really want to go Enola Holmes on this image, Forza games aren't D2D compatible.

We're thinking someone at Xbox might've messed up with this image. Announcements of this magnitude shouldn't be buried in an Xbox Insider update. Xbox should be shouting about it on the front page. So, why do an Xbox 360 game and two digital-only titles have D2D icons attached to them? I could think of a lazy reason.

Only time will tell, but consider us sceptical for now. We've chalked this one up to a blunder from Xbox, although it wouldn't surprise us if Xbox 360 games did eventually join the D2D programme. And hey, it's Xbox's birthday this Sunday. Maybe there's more to this than meets the eye.

@BacklogBrad the issue isn't with converting 360 or OG XBox game discs to digital versions, the issue is that those discs don't have a unique identifier assigned to them (this started with the XBox One generation, and not all of the early XBox One games have them).

Without the UID there's no way to assign a specific disc to the digital license, meaning one disc could be used to grant anyone digital access to that game. The UID prevents this as you need to revalidate the disc licence periodically, and if you sell the disc / lend it to someone, it will validate on their device, which will invalidate your license the next time your console does an online check in.

I hope they find a way to make it happen as it'd be awesome to add our XBox & 360 games to our digital libraries. Plus with this breakthrough it'd give Sony no reason not to follow suit and implementing a D2D feature of their own (i.e. Copy XBox's solution to the problem).

#4107. After a 16-year long dev period, Faraway, a shooting star arcade game about siphoning the energy of other stars, is out now

Lord almighty, video games take a while to make, 'ey? Especially if you're just one person working on it by yourself. Such is the case with Faraway, out today, an arcade game that reminds me of the early days of PS3 indies "about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive," all made single-handedly by creator of cult-classic mobile game Eliss, Steph Thirion. Did I mention that Faraway took 16 years to make? Like I said, game development is a lengthy process.

Looking at Faraway, and knowing how long it took to produce, it doesn't surprise me to come from a dev who managed to release a mobile game in the early days of the platform, long before free-to-play got its chokehold on the industry. It also really does feel like it should be sitting amongst the likes of PixelJunk, this thing should be something I'm desperate to play on my PS3 while I wait for my controller to charge.

As mentioned, you are a shooting star, a "spark meant to shine and vanish in a blink." But still you persist, connecting to and wrapping yourself around starts to "harvest their energy," in turn lengthening your own life, and of course, in arcadey fashion, racking up a nice score. It looks like game design as poetry, everything you're looking at procedurally generated to bring freshness to every run. I can fully envision this as a "one more run" kind of arcade game, the best kind, especially in an age long past the need to shove in another of your hard earned coins.

Faraway conceptually charms me because it taps into a style of game we don't get to see much of any more. What I'm saying is, I'm just a teensy bit sick of how many roguelikes there are, but that doesn't mean I don't want a game I can just hop in and out of at my own whims. Sure, arcade games might not be in vogue, I just miss them a bit. In any case, Faraway is available to pick up on Steam right now. Seems like it'll be worth a punt!

#4106. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4105. Dave The Diver's Latest Crossover Update Sees Another Beloved Indie Join The Fray

Since its arrival on Switch a few years back, Dave The Diver has crossed over with just about every other indie game imaginable (a slight exaggeration, but you get our point). Today, developer Mintrocket has announced yet another of these crossovers for its roster, as it is teaming up with Fireshine Games and Pugstorm on some new two-way Core Keeper content.

This crossover update launches on 30th November in both games, with the sandbox survival title gaining some new Blue Hole paraphernalia, and the beloved diving/bar management sim going all mine-y. It's all entirely optional, but it'll be hanging around permanently, so you are free to check it out whenever you fancy.

We'll start with Dave the Diver. As part of the crossover, the game will net a brand-new minigame, where you'll have to pick up a pickaxe and help defend Otto and Sammy's farm from hordes of Core Keeper Cavelings.

You'll be able to dive into the minigame after unlocking the farm through Sammy's VIP event, and there are new charms and figurine rewards for those who play.

The additions aren't quite as grand in Core Keeper, but they're very sweet, nonetheless. Cobra will arrive as a new underground merchant, selling all manner of Dave-themed goodies. There are Momo and Mini Dave pets, a new Bancho-inspired sushi armour, additional furniture items and sound effects, and more.

All of this will arrive in Core Keeper on all platforms on 30th November, while Mintrocket has confirmed that console rollout for the Dave the Diver update might be a little slower (though it will arrive on PC on 30th).

#4104. Former Xbox First-Party Game 'Kiln' Gets A New Identity And Its Biggest Update Of All Time

When Double Fine released Kiln as an Xbox first-party title last year, it's fair to say a lot of the Xbox fanbase was baffled by it. As much as it was a good game (we gave it a 7/10 in our Pure Xbox review), it also shipped with just a singular, online-only mode that was bound to get old pretty quickly.

Double Fine ended up being let go by Xbox, turning Kiln from an Xbox first-party game into an independent game, and it received a brand-new update back in September, adding a new creative game mode along with various other features.

But today, to mark the planned end of development, it's received its biggest update of all time - adding in three new game modes, an increased level cap, a Photo Booth and loads more besides.

Here's a look at just the highlights of this new update:

In terms of the three modes, Fire Fighter is a 4v4 mode where "both teams are in a mad dash to catch a flaming Chimenea", Stoked is also a 4v4 mode that's "all about igniting the Pyres with your team’s flame", and Local Mini Quench is a smaller version of the original Quench mode that can be played with up to three other people offline.

Offline mode is actually classed as a separate new feature as well:

"As part of being able to play locally, we’ve added an offline mode. This allows you to play and practice without needing to worry about your Ping or people. This, alongside the player hosted matches and account change, helps future-proof Kiln so that you can play it for years to come!"

Pretty cool, right? On top of that, Kiln has received a brand-new identity this week in the form of "Kiln: Reshaped", with the name change serving as a way to "let you know how much is in this update!".

Unfortunately, it does seem like Kiln's flame has already been doused for the majority of players at this point, but it's great to see Double Fine putting in the work to not only preserve it for the future, but hopefully light the spark once again for people who have fallen away from it in recent months.

Don't forget it's on Xbox Game Pass as well, or available on the Xbox Store for just £6.99 / $7.99.

#4103. Ablahshikar is a maximalist, sickos only salvage-survival CRPG about ripping organs out of warships and pawning off strange goods that's now out in early access

I don't know what's going on, and I like it

Sometimes, you come across a game and instantly know it's for the sickos. Today that is Ablahshikar, a "turn-based salvage-survival CRPG adrift on the Candle Sea" where you rip out the organs of enemy warships to "rebuild your vessel into a doomed chimera," that is out now in early access. To be honest I could have just called it a CRPG and still labelled it as a game for sickos, yet everything that's going on here is obviously just doubling down on the sick factor.

Ablahshikar is a particular flavour of maximalism. Having not played it, it feels a bit impossible describe, I mean, just have a read of some of the game's Steam page: "Lo, destiny crooks a finger only to those whose eyes peer beyond þe next tempest. Take custody of a faltering war-barge that wanders the outer brine of Dastgerd. Thy wrists y-braced to a wan terminal of bone-whyte and tarnysshed latoun, þou steerest Ablahshikar by murke point-nettes and sputteryng tables." I don't know what any of that means! And I love it. Reminds me of Hylics in that the game's world is not translating itself for its audience; you take what you're given, and you figure it out yourself.

Judging from trailers and screenshots, there's a mix of activities to be getting on with. Occasionally you'll be piloting a strange, not alien, but definitely ancient ship of some kind in an arcadey sort of fashion. Then occasionally there's something that resembles Caves of Qud, i.e. some odd, 2D maybe dungeon crawling where your moves are dictated by individual keys on your keyboard. Then there's Disco Elysiumy cutscenes that feel like a video game designed in the year 1200 by someone from the year 2200, aesthetically anyway. As I said, it is a particular flavour of maximalism.

Truthfully, I do not know if I am sicko enough for Ablahshikar. Its mighty vision is terrifying, but I certainly am curious about it. Right now it's less than a fiver, and it'll only be in early access for roughly a couple of months where the price will then go up, so perhaps it's best to get in at the ground floor. If you are one such sicko, then you can pick it up on Steam right here.

#4102. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4101. "That Was Very Tough" - Indiana Jones Dev Struggled To Transition From Gunplay

Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is one of the biggest surprises in recent years. Developer MachineGames, well known for its ability to make gunning down Nazis immensely satisfying in its Wolfenstein franchise, created what is arguably the best Indy adventure since The Last Crusade.

Yet transitioning from Wolfenstein wasn't exactly easy for the studio. In a new interview with the FRVR podcast (thanks, VGC), design director Jens Andersson explains how the developers found it "very tough" to focus on melee combat, given its expertise in gunplay.

“It was one of those features that we were so afraid of. Especially since MachineGames’ pedigree of Wolfenstein, coming into making Indiana Jones with a team primed to make more gore with heavy weapons, running and gunning… and then ‘oh, we’re going to make a family-friendly adventure’. That was very tough.”

Granted, 'family-friendly' might be a bit of a stretch given the game's 16+ PEGI rating, but we understand the sentiment. To make matters worse, MachineGames had to nail the balance between making guns a last resort for Indy while ensuring they still felt good to use.

“That was non-negotiable because we have a lot of people at Machine that love guns. They love everything about guns. They have people that professionally compete shooting. Gun Nuts. Obviously, you know, from Wolfenstein games that interest has been satiated. And at the game time, you have so many fans of Quake and other shooters out there. So we can’t make gunplay bad, that wouldn’t have been acceptable.”

To ensure that fans of guns still enjoyed the game, MachineGames strived to make melee combat "interesting, fun, and easy". This, combined with making reloading a fairly slow process, encourages you to experiment with your environment and locate more melee weapons.

#4100. BioWare are gone, but at least you'll be able to watch their final days in a documentary next year and oh wait that's really sad actually

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

In a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again."

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.

#4099. Forza Horizon 6 Content Roadmap Revealed For Late 2026 & 2027

With a specific focus on January and February of next year

Ready for some more news on Forza Horizon 6? The team at Playground Games has announced a content roadmap for the game today, pulling the curtain back on their plans for the end of 2026 and all of next year.

You can get loads of detail about all of this in the video up above, but in a nutshell, we're getting Series 8 "Horizon Holidays" and Series 9 "Legendary Explorers" before the year is out. Then, as we head into January and February, Series 10 will be based around "Exotics and Tuners", while other new additions include a permanent new radio station, absolutely loads of new Reward Cars, and various other bits and bobs.

Most importantly, the first expansion for the game will also be released in January of 2027. Playground Games still doesn't want to talk about it just yet, but apparently we'll be hearing about it very soon.

News Forza Horizon 6's First Premium Expansion Planned For January 2027 Alongside PS5 Launch

Sony fans loved FH5, will they vibe with FH6? Probably

As you can see from the rest of this roadmap, the remainder of 2027 gets more vague for now, but it's confirmed that a second expansion is on the way along with a Festival Playlist overhaul, new race routes and various other new features.

They do talk quite a lot about the Festival Playlist overhaul in the video up above, so again, it's well worth a watch if you want to know more about what's on the way to Forza Horizon 6 in the future.

All of this sounds pretty good to us, and considering how the game has come in for a little bit of disgruntlement in recent months, it's clear to see that Playground Games is hoping for a strong 2027 when it comes to new FH6 content.

#4098. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4097. Take on a time-manipulating corporation in the very Soul Eater meets Jet Set Radio action roguelite CHRONO PUNK

Plus a little bit of Spider-Man, Devil May Cry and Kingdom Hearts

My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from said era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are big and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

#4095. PSA: Xbox And GTA 6 Have Both Pushed Out Small New Updates

One's a console update, the other potentially a "day one" patch

As we get ready to wrap up the working week here at Pure Xbox, we wanted to alert you to a couple of new updates that have been pushed out in recent days - one for Xbox consoles in general, and another specifically for GTA 6.

The Xbox console update was actually released on Wednesday, but nobody made a song and dance about it whatsoever, while the patch notes only referenced "general stability and performance improvements".

However, we now know that the update was related to the addition of achievements in four original Xbox games, and unless you download the update, you won't be able to see those achievements right now.

There's a chance your console may have downloaded this automatically but to check, go to "Settings", "System", "Updates" and then see if there's an update waiting to be downloaded or not.

News Four OG Xbox Games Are Getting Achievements For The First Time Ever

"We’re introducing one of the top requested features"

As for GTA 6, in addition to the 200GB+ preload that went live a few days ago, there's also now a new update as of a few hours ago that sits at around 2.2GB. You'll need to download this in order to start playing on November 19th.

Some people are speculating that this might be the so-called "day one patch", but who knows whether we might get another one between now and next Thursday. In any case, you'll want to get this queued up as soon as possible (unless you haven't installed the game yet, in which case it'll be included in your initial download).

There's a chance you may see a different size, but it's somewhere around that 2.2GB mark. We're also spotting that some people haven't got it yet for whatever reason, but it should roll out to all Xbox users in the very near future.

Don't forget that Alpha Skip-Ahead Xbox Insiders have also received a special new update this week that adds three new features for testing purposes, so if you're part of the Insider programme, keep an eye out for that.

We'll be back next week with loads more coverage on the GTA 6 launch, and here's hoping there are no more downloads to get us ready for November 19th. Just a few more sleeps until the big day!

#4094. After taking over EA, Saudi Arabia and their private equity cronies have reportedly held talks about buying Unity

The engine builders have, it's claimed, been working with an investment ​bank to evaluate [their] options

Members of the consortium led by the Saudi Arabian government's Public Investment Fund and some private equity suits which took over EA this year in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion reportedly have a new target in their sights. Unity, software company and makers of the game engine bearing the same name, have held talks with the consortium over a potential takeover, it's claimed.

According to Reuters, a consortium including Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and private equity firm Silver Lake Partners recently approached Unity about a deal that would value the company at around $25 billion. Unity are, it's claimed, currently working with an investment bank to evaluate their options following the chat, with no deal set in stone right now.

Silver Lake, Reuters note, are already among Unity's largest shareholders and invested up to $400 million in the engine builders in 2017. In fact, Silver Lake's managing director and CEO Egon Durban already has a seat on Unity's board of directors, so will probably have to butt out of any takeover talks.

Assuming the consortium would go the leveraged buyout route, loading Unity up with debt like the EA takeover did, it's hard to see any deal not resulting in similarly catastrophic consequences for those working at Unity. EA laid off a reported 400 people in an effort to cut costs after coming under the boot of the Saudi state and private equity, shutting BioWare and cancelling something Sims-related codenamed Project Lotus. BioWare's demise has since been reported to have largely come down to EA execs not wanting to fund both Star Wars Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, with them opting to back only Battlefront 3.

Unity's recent financial results are looking strong, propped up by year-on-year growth in an AI-powered ad network dubbed Vector, so one would assume that bit of the business likely wouldn't be top of the list if any bloodletting was to end up happening.

Solidarity to any Unity workers who're now having to live under the shadow of this prospective takeover and the upheaval it could lead to if it goes ahead in a fashion which mirrors the EA deal.

#4093. "It's a brave new world": GTA 6's PC port will release sooner than you think to avoid losing money to AI rip-offs, says former Rockstar tech director

"If it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it."

GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it launches on 19th November. In general, Vermeij thinks that how to avoid having your games duplicated by chatbot herders is "the big question" right now for devs and publishers, particularly those who don't have the means to enforce their intellectual property dominions as vehemently as Take-Two do for Grand Theft Auto.

Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved. He shared a sweary anecdote about the company's difficulties getting the original GTA 1 to look the business on Sony's PlayStation.

"I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the company at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he said. "So they worked on PC and then an external company in Dundee did the PlayStation version. Which was really weird, because like, PCs were so much more powerful - still the case, but in those days, it was even more so.

"And I remember, at the time, the GTA team was definitely the most rowdy of all of the teams," Vermeij continued. "And there was one particular day where they sent the PC build away, and then it came back from the PlayStation people, and they had cut down all the textures from 256 colours to 16 colours, and my god, the artist was just going around and swearing - 'what the fuck did they do to our textures, I can't believe it, we can't release this shite'. So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console. So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better."

When it came time to develop GTA 3, Rockstar "flipped that around", Vermeij went on, creating the console versions first. "Clearly the PC market has sort of grown, caught up with the console market, but there's still that same mindset," he said. Most publishers prefer to release all versions at once, Vermeij added, "because then there's only one marketing campaign they have to pay for." GTA lives by its own rules, however. "I guess it's less of an argument for them because the game is just so big, so they just kind of always left it that way. And for developers, it's way easier to just do one version at a time. So, you know, that makes sense."

The arrival of generative AI threatens to throw all this to the winds. Tools such as Reverse Engineer Anything allow for speedy unofficial ports or "slopcomps" of console games on PC, despite warnings from seasoned recomp developers that using genAI for this purpose wrecks the community aspect of unofficial porting, and results in illegible "bruteforce" code rather than preserving some understanding of how the original game was made.

"It really has changed the world," Vermeij observed, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

GTA 6 is, according to Rockstar and Take-Two at least, an enormously fiddly production, costing hundreds of millions of dollars over eight years in development. Nonetheless, Vermeij thinks current genAI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a port. "It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things. And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it."

There are already signs that genAI PC port goldrushers are ready to pounce on GTA 6. Just today, Ars Technica reported on efforts to yassify the game's PS5 trailer footage by piping it through a stronker PC graphics card and using Nvidia's DLSS 5 to apply extra layers of gloss.

Vermeij himself left Rockstar way back in 2009 and is now an indie developer. His current early access project is Plentiful, a hexagonal god sim with an emphasis on water physics. It uses "AI-assisted machine translation for localization", but not for "gameplay content, art, or audio". Vermeij is, in general, interested in generative AI despite the surging tide of slopcomp ports. Smaller indie developers are, of course, more vulnerable to the financial fallout from having their work unofficially cloned by generative AI, but Vermeij thinks it's an existential worry for megacorps like Take-Two as well.

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest," he told me in closing. "I don't see it. But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you said, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job. But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out."

The latest rumour-mongering places GTA 6's PC release sometime in early 2027. In other news, Rockstar staff are soon to formally vote on whether to apply for union recognition. If the organisers carry the day, the resulting union could encompass nearly all the company's UK staff below management level.

#4092. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4091. Steam gets a boatload of restored Wing Commanders and Ultima ports after EA producer stumbles across cupboard of old tapes

"He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones"

EA have stuck a bunch of restored versions and ports of classic games, on Steam, GOG and the EA App. 25 games in all, including multiple entries in the Wing Commander and Ultima series, are part of the haul. Why's this happening now? Well, an EA producer stumbled across a cupboard full of old tapes, film reels and CDs.

According to an interview with The Game Business, the discovery of this old gubbins was a consequence of EA senior producer Jim Vessella needing somewhere new to stick a bunch of Betacam tapes used to help make the Command & Conquer Remastered Collection. "One of the facilities people was like, 'I think there’s a room in the other building that has a couple of items like that'," Vessella recalled. "He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones… just, whoa. Knowing what I’d discovered with the Command & Conquer tapes, I really felt like we had to find out what was on all these tapes."

The producer was able to convince EA's bosses that this stuff was worth the work needed to stick it back on storefronts, and lo, an EA blog post gushing about their vault's door having slid aside to reveal this pile of retro games.
